content: Modern C++ guidance (post-C++11) recommends a function-local static (Meyers singleton / magic static) for thread-safe one-time construction of a shared primitive, and std::call_once/std::once_flag for one-time initialization logic; double-checked locking is discouraged as unnecessary since C++11. For a lock acquired repeatedly (not one-time init), the correct pattern is a magic-static std::mutex& accessor plus a plain std::lock_guard at each call site -- call_once itself is for one-time actions, not a repeatable critical-section guard.
